## Why

DocumentCloud and MuckRock host the released-ALPR-materials surface the
I6/I7 discovery named (police-department document releases and the public
FOIA request pages behind them). The materials are *public
unauthenticated pages*, but the served bytes routinely carry uploader
names, descriptions and agency text that are Part VIII-protected — so the
connector's deliverable is a **screened, redacted rendition** plus the
upstream URL and the original's digest, never the raw page. Where no
reliable redaction exists the row is a recorded refusal, not a stored raw
(the ticket's verbatim rule). The MuckRock ToS governs DocumentCloud and
is affirmatively restrictive toward automated extraction, so the source
rows land gated: leg A's bounded GETs are queued under GATE-G5's OM-20
naming (not executed — see deferrals); leg B (the first real wire as a
connector run) is the operator's OP-26 act — staged, never performed.

## What ships

- **`connectors/documentcloud.py`** — the `documentcloud` connector
  (eight-stage). `discover()` walks exactly the committed
  `data/documentcloud_targets.toml` inventory (a binding outside it
  refuses loud). `fetch()` = one polite GET per target through
  `ctx.fetcher` only (host opt-out → target opt-out → politeness →
  interstitial check → kind dispatch → in-memory Part VIII screen →
  admit), each outcome recorded on the connector's per-target ledger.
  Six bounded kinds: `api_document` / `api_project` (the public
  DocumentCloud API JSON lookups), `document_page` / `project_page`
  (the public `www.documentcloud.org` uploader pages — meta only),
  `muckrock_page` (the public `/foi/…` request page — status marker +
  linkage), `terms_page` (the governing ToS — verbatim bounded capture).
  `capture()` persists ONLY the screened records: a `FetchResult` that
  never passed the screen is refused; the served page's own bytes are
  never stored.
- **The rendition machinery** — `_build_rendition` walks the allowlisted
  fields, screens each candidate under its declared hazard name
  (`screen_as` — contributor/author→`name`, description/source→`description`/`notes`),
  redacts a hit in memory (name + classes + value sha256 into
  `redacted_fields`, names-only `refused_fields`), then screens the
  whole canonical record again: residual hits →
  `sig.documentcloud-refusal/1` (pointer + counts + hash — the content
  itself is dropped); clean → `sig.documentcloud-rendition/1`
  (allowlisted fields + redaction provenance + uploader page URL +
  original sha256 + byte size).
- **Committed data** — `data/documentcloud_targets.toml`
  (`sig.documentcloud-targets/1`: 11 seeds — 4 `api_document`, 3
  `api_project`, 2 public DocumentCloud pages, the `muckrock.com/tos/`
  terms page and the public MuckRock request page `136412`; each row is
  URL + kind + source + evidence ref, never content; fail-closed on
  drift — schema/count/sort/https/public-path) +
  `data/documentcloud_vocab.toml` (`sig.documentcloud-vocab/1`: the
  four-predicate allowlist, forbidden genres, the six kinds' reviewed
  public path patterns, the committed host set, terms element ids,
  interstitial markers, MuckRock status vocabulary, the `screen_as`
  hazard-name map).
- **Registry wiring** — `sources.toml`: the `muckrock_public` row
  appended (custody posture recorded, `public_terms_only`,
  `ingestion_permitted=false`, rights UNDETERMINED/`review_needed`) and
  the pre-existing `documentcloud` row's notes updated to name this
  connector path — its gated, unresolved-rights posture preserved
  verbatim; `live_targets.toml` + `live_targets.py` expand the
  `documentcloud_targets` kind per source; `runner.py`
  `CONNECTOR_FOR_SOURCE` maps both source ids + the fixture-run
  target-resolution set; `__init__.py` registers the module. The
  authenticated `muckrock` api_v2 row (the `records` connector's own
  gated lane) is untouched.
- **Screen membership** — `ops/at_rest_audit.toml`: the new source's
  lane membership appended, including the S6 records-derived handling;
  the connector consumes the SAME committed declaration through
  `evidence.screen` — no drifted copy.
- **Claims** — allowlisted to exactly four predicates
  (`released_documents`, `platform`, `acquisition_method`, `title`),
  every claim carrying `uploader_page` (the public page behind the
  release); index records are `document_index`/`collection_index`,
  captures are `evidence_artifact` rows with integrity
  `screened_rendition`, plus `terms_capture`, `capture_refusal` and
  per-capture `quality_report` rows. A denied field name in emitted
  facts fails loud (`PredicateNotAllowed` family) — never a warning.
- **Tests** — `tests/connectors/test_documentcloud.py` (29) + committed
  fixtures under `tests/connectors/fixtures/documentcloud/`. Zero
  network — a `FakeTransport` serves canned pages through a real
  `PoliteFetcher`.
- **Leg-A queue + leg-B packet** —
  `docs/build/reports/rights/p3677/leg-a-queue.toml` (11 legs, all
  `queued`/`prepared_not_executed`, blocker recorded) +
  `leg-b-packet.md` (the operator's first-wire act staged —
  agent-drafted, go lines blank).

## Deviations / deferrals

1. **The ticket's `I7-C13` label names no catalog record** — the
   discovery evidence the ticket cites is `decision_catalog.csv` row
   **I7-C2** (DocumentCloud/MuckRock, "existing refused channel"
   posture) plus the I6/I7 candidate rows (I7-U645/U669/U681, I6-C031).
   Recorded honestly in the inventory's `source_ref` — the seed set
   cites the verbatim evidence ids, never an invented catalog row.
2. **Persisted artifact = the screened record, never the served page**
   (ADR-185's strongest read — same posture as P36.74/P36.76). The raw
   page is fetched once, parsed + screened in memory, dropped; document
   binaries (pdf/full_text/asset URLs) are recorded as pointers only —
   never fetched.
3. **Leg A's GETs queued** — `live_verification=false` dispatch + the
   probe-UA precondition fails (`live:P35.38a`: `/data-collection/` 404
   at 2026-10-27T07:54:48Z, root 200 — SIG-INGEST-036 forbids a
   descriptive UA citing a dead owned page). **D-P36.77-1** (kind V,
   OPEN) carries the 11 legs; the OM-19 re-run prompt is recorded
   verbatim.
4. **Leg B held** — **D-P36.77-2** (kind V, OPEN): the operator's
   OP-26 act; the packet is staged `prepared_not_executed`.
5. **Size budget overage recorded** (~2,900 non-generated/non-fixture
   lines vs the S ≤1,500 band — connector 1,551 + tests 728 + data 289 +
   queue/packet 237 + wiring ~130) — same posture as P36.74/P36.76's
   recorded overages; the docstring-heavy policy surface and the
   refusal-kind records are what reviewers audit.
6. **Obligation-tooling note** — `obligation_events.py append`
   deadlocks on a ticket opening two DEFERRALS rows at once (each
   anchor's pre-check is blocked by the other row's missing anchor);
   the second row's anchor was appended after staging its row exactly as
   P36.76 recorded — chain `check` verified green.
